title: Student Placement Prediction System
summary: End-to-end full-stack cascaded ML pipeline deployed to predict student placements and provide personalized LLM feedback.
problem: Predicting student placement outcomes on a 100K+ records dataset requires careful algorithmic choice to avoid data leakage and strong deployment strategy to make the predictions accessible.
solution: Trained and benchmarked 6 models to identify XGBoost (Recall: 0.63) as the best classifier and Linear Regression (R2: 0.79) as the best regressor. Deployed a cascaded pipeline with a shared preprocessor.
architecture: A full-stack deployment on Render using a FastAPI backend to serve the ML cascaded models and Groq Llama 3.1 LLM, interfaced via a Streamlit frontend.
technical_decisions: Selected a cascaded classification + regression strategy rather than a multi-output model to maintain distinct thresholds. Chosen Groq API for Llama 3.1 inference due to its extreme low latency generation suitable for web interaction.
implementation: 100K student records processed. Shared preprocessor developed to eliminate data leakage between train/test splits and deployment states. Deployed to Render.
challenges: A major challenge was preventing data leakage between the two sequential models while keeping the API endpoints stateless and fast.
results: Regressed salary with Linear Regression R2: 0.79
lessons: Learned that cascaded ML models require strict state preservation of standard scalers and encoding to guarantee correct inference behavior in production APIs.

title: Credit Card Fraud Detection
summary: High-performance classifier targeting an aggressively imbalanced financial dataset to minimize false negatives.
problem: Fraud detection datasets show extreme class imbalance (only 0.17% fraud rate), meaning naive accuracy is a misleading metric and models inherently lean toward the majority class.
solution: Applied SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique) to address class imbalance, improving the fraud detection rate by 35%.
architecture: Structured Jupyter pipeline focusing heavily on exploratory data analysis, SMOTE application, hyperparameter tuning grid search, and multi-model benchmarking.
technical_decisions: Optimized strictly for Recall and F1-score rather than accuracy to minimize false negatives (which are unacceptable in fraud detection).
implementation: Benchmarked Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, and XGBoost on the resampled data to establish the strongest discriminator.
challenges: Over-representing synthetic data can lead to poor test generalization. Ensured SMOTE was applied strictly to the training split, not validation.
results: Demonstrated 35% improvement in detection rate on 0.17% fraud rate data
lessons: Discovered that SMOTE creates synthetic overlap logic that standard tree ensembles can occasionally overfit; rigorous independent validation sets are required.

title: Quillify – AI Writing Assistant
summary: Multi-module AI writing assistant integrating large language models for SEO and structural editing.
problem: Many LLM wrappers lack focused constraints. Standard chat interfaces don't perform well for specialized multi-step text pipeline tasks like SEO optimization coupled with tone editing.
solution: Architecting a multi-module assistant targeting specific domain functions: Blog SEO Analyzer, Paragraph Enhancer, Resume Optimizer, and Tone Rewriter.
architecture: Expected to utilize a FastAPI orchestration layer interacting with Gemini via LangChain, utilizing spaCy/KeyBERT for deterministic NLP rule parsing before generating.
technical_decisions: Combining deterministic NLP (spaCy/KeyBERT) with generative LLMs (Gemini API) to anchor and score text explicitly before passing instructions to the LLM.
implementation: Currently in progress. Designing keyword extraction and content scoring logic components.
challenges: Ensuring the output from LangChain handles unstructured inputs without breaking the strict JSON schema required for multiple internal API modules.
lessons: Understanding the limits of relying purely on generative AI versus utilizing structured deterministic analysis like KeyBERT for feature extraction.

title: Heart Disease Prediction
summary: Interactive data dashboard and predictive model for heart disease risk classification.
problem: Medical models require interpretable interfaces for users to understand prediction thresholds.
solution: Deployed a Streamlit application providing interactive health inputs against a trained Scikit-learn model.
architecture: Monolithic Streamlit application embedding the pickled classification model and Plotly for visual feedback.
technical_decisions: Leveraged Plotly for highly interactive dashboard metrics alongside the raw prediction probability.
implementation: Trained on the UCI dataset (303 patients, 13 features), deployed via Streamlit cloud.
challenges: Balancing limited feature permutations against interactive dashboard requirements for edge cases.
results: Deployed publicly with Plotly interactive charts
lessons: Streamlit proves highly effective for extremely fast ML prototyping and basic dashboard interactions.
